narrative:
Your application was denied because the model estimated an 80% probability that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. In practical terms, the review treated your profile as high-risk for bar failure, so admission was not extended.

The strongest factor was your third-year class standing: you were in the first decile, far below the accepted-student average near the sixth decile. This pushed the prediction strongly toward failure. The second most influential factor was your LSAT score of 19.30, which is well below the accepted-student average of 37.18; this also pushed toward failure. The third factor was your first-year class standing, again first decile compared with an accepted average near the sixth decile, which added further risk. Your undergraduate GPA of 3.20 is close to the accepted average of 3.23, so it was not a main reason for denial.

To improve your chances, speak with admissions about their concerns, ask what evidence would strengthen a future application, and consider retaking the LSAT if you can prepare substantially. You should also address your early class standing directly, show any upward trend or serious circumstances, and reapply only when you can present stronger academic and test evidence.
